guide.tsautocraft.overview.title: Overview
guide.tsautocraft.overview.text:
This mod adds AE2-style autocrafting to Tom's Simple Storage. You teach the network recipes with patterns, and it crafts what you request - including all intermediate steps.

Blocks:
- Pattern Terminal: storage terminal that encodes patterns.
- Pattern Provider: holds patterns and fills crafters and machines.
- Autocrafting Terminal: runs and lists crafting jobs.
- Pattern Access Terminal: all patterns of the network in one GUI.
- Requester / Level Maintainer: keep items stocked.
- Crafting Emitter: redstone signal by item amount or job demand.
- Exporter / Importer: move items between the network and inventories.
- Upgrades: Capacity, Speed, Stack, Crafting, Redstone.

All blocks must be connected to the same Tom's Inventory Cable network as an Inventory Connector. Turn the page or use the contents.
guide.tsautocraft.setup.title: Minimal setup
guide.tsautocraft.setup.text:
1. Build a Tom's storage: Inventory Connector next to chests, Inventory Cables from it.
2. Connect an Autocrafting Terminal (runs the jobs) and a Pattern Terminal to the cables.
3. Place a Pattern Provider on the cable network and a vanilla Crafter next to it.
4. Let the crafter drop its result into a chest and put an Importer (connected to the cables) on that chest, so results go back into storage.
5. The crafter needs a trigger: build your own redstone circuit, put a Redstone Upgrade into the provider, or set crafterTrigger to direct or redstone in the config.
6. Encode a crafting pattern in the Pattern Terminal and put it into the provider.
7. The item now shows a green + in every terminal. Ctrl + click it, enter an amount, Calculate, Start.
guide.tsautocraft.pattern_terminal.title: Pattern Terminal
guide.tsautocraft.pattern_terminal.text:
A Tom's storage terminal (search, sorting, tall mode) with an encoding area instead of a crafting grid.

- Mode button (left): crafting, processing, smelting, fluid, brewing (and modes of other mods).
- Grid: ghost items, nothing is used up. In crafting mode one item per slot and the result is computed. In free modes left click with a stack sets its size, right click adds/removes one.
- Outputs: set by hand in free modes.
- x2, /2, x10, /10 (right of the encoding area, free modes only): scale all amounts at once. Greyed out when an amount would exceed 999 or stop being a whole number.
- S: substitutes on/off (crafting only, any item that gives the same result may be used).
- X: clear grid, L: load the pattern in the blank slot back into the grid.
- Put Blank Patterns into the top slot and press Encode. A named pattern keeps its name when re-encoded.
guide.tsautocraft.pattern_provider.title: Pattern Provider
guide.tsautocraft.pattern_provider.text:
Holds patterns (9 slots, +9 per Capacity Upgrade up to 36) and delivers the inputs to machines when a job needs them.

- Full block: supplies every adjacent crafter or machine, one after the other. A redstone pulse only goes to the machine that was just filled.
- Connector (and framed connector): supplies only the block it faces.
- Crafting patterns fill a vanilla Crafter in pattern order. Processing patterns insert all inputs at once or nothing.
- Blocking mode: only push again once no inputs are left in the machine.
- Lock mode: off, until result returned (waits for the Importer), or with/without redstone signal.
- Priority: providers with a higher priority are used first.
- Results must come back through an Importer (or directly into storage).
- Upgrades: Capacity, Speed, Stack, Redstone.
Runs the crafting jobs of the network; at least one is needed. It lists all craftable items and all jobs on the network.

- Select an item, enter an amount and request it.
- Each job shows its progress; hover for the steps and why one waits (missing items, busy provider).
- Buttons per job: priority (high/normal/low), pause, cancel. When a job is cancelled, inputs still inside machines can be returned (config returnInputsOnCancel).
- Tabs Running/History: the history lists the last finished or cancelled jobs (✕ clears it), running jobs show the estimated time left in their tooltip.
- Jobs reserve their materials, so two jobs never use the same items.
- Capacity Upgrades allow more parallel jobs.
guide.tsautocraft.requesting.title: Requesting items
guide.tsautocraft.requesting.text:
Craftable items show a green + in every Tom's terminal on the network.

- Ctrl + click a craftable item, or click one with amount 0, to open the request dialog.
- Enter the amount and press Calculate: you get a material list (from storage, to craft, missing); the Tree/List button shows the recipe tree instead (click a line to expand or collapse it).
- Start begins the job. If something is missing, a button offers the largest amount that can be crafted now.
- In Tom's Crafting Terminal the recipe viewer + button can craft missing ingredients (Ctrl + click).
guide.tsautocraft.pattern_access_termina: Shows the pattern slots of every Pattern Provider on the cable network in one GUI. Insert, take out and swap patterns without walking to each provider. The search box filters by provider name or pattern output; name providers in an anvil to find them easily. It holds no items itself.
guide.tsautocraft.requester.title: Requester
guide.tsautocraft.requester.text: Keeps up to 6 items at a minimum stock. Set an item and a target amount per entry; when the stock in the network drops below it, a job for the difference starts automatically. Only one job per entry runs at a time, so nothing is crafted twice while results are still inside machines. Recipe viewer: + or drag an item onto an entry.
guide.tsautocraft.level_maintainer.title: Level Maintainer
guide.tsautocraft.level_maintainer.text:
Like the Requester, but with 12 entries of item, threshold and batch size: when the stock (minus what other jobs reserved) drops below the threshold, a job for the batch amount starts. One job per entry at a time.

Upgrades: Speed (shorter check interval), Redstone (maintain only with or without a signal, or toggle on pulses; running jobs always continue).
guide.tsautocraft.crafting_emitter.title: Crafting Emitter
guide.tsautocraft.crafting_emitter.text:
Gives a redstone signal depending on one item of the network:
- below: while the stock is below the amount,
- above: while the stock is at least the amount,
- craft: the item counts as craftable and the signal is on while a job needs it - e.g. to switch on a farm. The items must come back through an Importer or into storage.

The full block emits on all sides. The directional (and framed directional) variant only emits out of its front.
guide.tsautocraft.exporter_importer.text:
Exporter: pushes filtered items from the network into the inventory it faces (without filters nothing happens). Items reserved by jobs are never exported. With a Crafting Upgrade, missing filter items are crafted.

Importer: pulls items from the inventory it faces into the network; no filter = everything. It also reports results of jobs, so put it on the output chest behind crafters and machines.

Filters: plain items are ghost items; Tom's filter items are real items. Modes: round robin, priority, random, and blacklist (Importer). Upgrades: Speed, Stack, Redstone. Framed variants can be painted with Tom's Paint Kit.
guide.tsautocraft.upgrades.title: Upgrades
guide.tsautocraft.upgrades.text:
Upgrades go into the panel on the right of the GUI; several of the same kind stack in one slot.

- Capacity: Autocrafting Terminal more parallel jobs; Pattern Provider 9 more pattern slots.
- Speed: Importer/Exporter shorter interval; Pattern Provider one more delivery per tick; Level Maintainer shorter check interval.
- Stack: Importer/Exporter 4x more items per operation; Pattern Provider 4x more crafts per delivery (up to 64).
- Crafting: Exporter crafts missing filter items.
- Redstone: Importer/Exporter/Level Maintainer work only with or without a signal or toggle on pulses; Pattern Provider pulses the machine after every delivery.
guide.tsautocraft.mode_crafting.title: Mode: Crafting
guide.tsautocraft.mode_crafting.text: For the vanilla Crafter. One item per grid slot; the result is computed from the recipe. The provider puts the items into crafter slots 0-8 in pattern order (shifted to enabled slots if some are disabled, see config). Without blocking mode, more sets of the same recipe are stacked on top. With substitutes on, any item that gives the same result may be used per slot (e.g. other planks). How the crafter is triggered depends on the config (crafterTrigger).
guide.tsautocraft.mode_processing.title: Mode: Processing
guide.tsautocraft.mode_processing.text:
For any machine with an inventory. Free amounts for up to 9 inputs and 3 outputs set by hand (use x2, /2, x10, /10 to scale them). The provider inserts all inputs at once or nothing. The outputs must come back through an Importer. Machine profiles (datapack) can define which sides get the items (also different sides for different inputs), a redstone pulse, a pause between deliveries and blocking per machine.

Example (picture): water bottles. A Pattern Provider Connector fills a dispenser that faces a water source, pattern 1 glass bottle -> 1 water bottle. The built-in dispenser profile gives the dispenser a redstone pulse after every delivery, so it fills the bottle; an Importer with a water bottle as filter takes it out.
guide.tsautocraft.mode_smelting.title: Mode: Smelting
guide.tsautocraft.mode_smelting.text: For furnaces, blast furnaces and smokers. The first grid item is the input; the result comes from the furnace recipe. Fuel is up to you (e.g. a hopper or Exporter feeding coal). Results come back through an Importer on the furnace or below it.
guide.tsautocraft.mode_fluid.title: Mode: Fluid processing
guide.tsautocraft.mode_fluid.text: Tom's storage has no fluids, so fluids travel as filled containers (buckets, bottles). Like processing, but filled containers are emptied into the machine's fluid tank and the empty containers go back into the network. An Importer with a filled container as filter fills empty containers from the machine back into the network.
guide.tsautocraft.mode_brewing.title: Mode: Brewing
guide.tsautocraft.mode_brewing.text:
For the brewing stand. In this mode the Pattern Terminal grid looks like the brewing stand: fuel top left (optional), reagent top middle, 1-3 bottles in the bottom row (they may differ); the results are computed from the brewing recipes, mod and datapack recipes included.

The provider fills an empty stand: bottles and reagent every brew, the fuel only when the fuel slot is empty (it is not counted per brew, one blaze powder lasts 20 brews). JEI/REI "+" encodes a full stand. The Importer waits until the brew is done, so it never takes unfinished potions.
guide.tsautocraft.jei.title: JEI and REI
guide.tsautocraft.jei.text:
- Pattern Terminal: the + button fills the grid with the recipe (mode is chosen from the recipe type), or drag items onto grid slots.
- Pattern Provider: + encodes the recipe directly into a free slot, using a Blank Pattern from your inventory.
- Requester: + puts the recipe output into an entry; drag items onto entries.
- Exporter/Importer: drag items onto filter slots.
- Tom's Crafting Terminal: + with Ctrl + click crafts missing ingredients.
REI works like JEI (less tested).
guide.tsautocraft.config.title: Configuration
guide.tsautocraft.config.text:
File config/tsautocraft.json, or the Mod Menu config screen.

- crafterTrigger: external (your own redstone circuit, default), direct (block tick) or redstone (2-tick pulse from the provider).
- enableDisabledCrafterSlots: use disabled crafter slots instead of shifting the recipe.
- Crafter timings, provider lock timeout, return inputs on cancel.
- Jobs per Autocrafting Terminal and per Capacity Upgrade, largest request, job timeouts, history size.
- Requester, Level Maintainer and Importer/Exporter intervals and amounts.
Machines can be configured by datapack: data/<namespace>/tsautocraft/machines/*.json.
tooltip.tsautocraft.brewing.fuel: Fuel (optional): only delivered when the stand's fuel slot is empty, not counted per brew
msg.tsautocraft.encode.no_brewing_fuel: Top left is the fuel slot: this item is no brewing fuel
